Thanks — Wednesday works for me. Confirming details for the proposal:
- We want a 10% holdback (billed as a standby credit model: only charged if Redwood activates those GPUs during exceptional bursts).
- Min active GPU should be set so that our conversational latency SLOs are met (we estimated 40 concurrent tokens/sec on p4d-like instances), but we are open to Redwood suggesting the exact min number based on your runtime profiling.
- Ramp window: 3 stages over 8 weeks (week 0: baseline, week 3: +30%, week 7: full commit). Each stage gated by load tests + error/latency checks.

Please include a short operational note about how prewarming and KV cache warmup is managed during stage transitions. That matters for our product team.

— Anna

Subject: Draft proposal: GPU holdback mechanics + staged activation (attached)

Anna — attaching our draft proposal (redwood_proposal_gpu_holdback_v1.pdf) and a short appendix describing activation controls. Summary below.

Attachment: redwood_proposal_gpu_holdback_v1.pdf (proposal, includes pricing table and SLA notes)
Other attachment referenced: orchidai_demand_forecast_q3.xlsx (received)

Proposal summary (three configurable options):

1) Steady baseline (Conservative)
- Cluster: 16 nodes x 8x A100-80GB equiv = 128 GPUs
- Min active GPUs: 96 (75% of cluster)
- Holdback: 12 GPUs (9.4% of cluster) retained as "standby"; Redwood will only charge holdback prorated if used beyond a 15-minute sustained activation window.
- Ramp: baseline -> +25% at week 4 -> +50% at week 8 (gates: load test pass, error rate <1.5%, latency P95 within target)

2) Growth baseline (Balanced)
- Cluster: 24 nodes x 8x A100 = 192 GPUs
- Min active GPUs: 144 (75%)
- Holdback: 18 GPUs (9.4%) with same billing mechanics; option to convert holdback to active capacity after week 5 with 7-day notice and pro-rated billing adjustments.

3) Staircase (Aggressive)
- Cluster: start with 96 GPUs (12 nodes) then staged scale to 192 GPUs over 6 weeks using automated lane activation.
- Min active GPUs: 72 initially; holdback 10% that can be temporarily activated for bursts with a cap of 2x for up to 6 hours/day.

Operational notes:
- Prewarm and KV cache: Redwood will run background prewarm jobs during stage transitions; we recommend a 24–48 hour soft ramp window to allow cache warmup for high-embedding reuse flows.
- Canary gating: Canary traffic routed to a subset of nodes with tracing hooks enabled; rollback policy if error or token cost regressions exceed thresholds.
- Autoscaling behavior: dedicated lane retains min active GPUs; autoscaler will favor warmed nodes before cold starts to minimize latency spikes.

Commercial/credits:
- For the first 60 days, holdback is billed at 20% of the active GPU rate as a standby fee; any activation beyond standby window billed at full rate but Redwood offers a one-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of first month usage if no activation occurred.

Next steps:
- Review this draft w/ your infra and product teams on Wed 6/18 10:00am PT (confirmed).
- If accepted, we’ll issue a DocuSign with the agreed option, including clauses for holdback conversion and activation triggers.

— Karthik Iyer
Lead Capacity Architect, Redwood Inference
